title: Catch and Release (Verbose Log-and-Reraise)
pattern: Intermediate layers of a call stack catch every error variant, write a redundant log entry, and immediately re-raise or return the exact same error unchanged.
why_bad: It bloats the codebase with duplicate error-handling code, tightly couples intermediate functions to specific lower-level error types, and floods system logs with multiple duplicate, non-actionable entries for a single failure.
detection: `match` blocks or `.map_err()` calls whose only action in the error branch is to call a logging macro before returning the error unaltered.
fix: Allow the error to propagate naturally up the call stack to a single centralized boundary handler that logs the error once with its full backtrace.
source: Andrew Hunt & David Hurst Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer*, Topic 24 ("Catch and Release is for Fish").
